## 2024-03-24 - Fix XSS Vulnerability in QR Code Generation
**Vulnerability:** The application used `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to render SVG strings generated by `qrcode-generator` directly into the DOM. While the input to the QR code is intended to be a URL, using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` inherently opens a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vector if the input is ever malformed or maliciously crafted.
**Learning:** `qrcode-generator` provides multiple output formats. Generating raw SVG tags requires risky HTML injection, whereas generating a Data URL (`createDataURL`) allows rendering via a standard, safe `<img>` tag.
**Prevention:** Avoid `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` whenever possible. Always prefer native DOM element properties (like `src` on an `img`) over raw HTML injection, especially when dealing with data that includes user-provided or URL-derived content.
